title: All-SEC forward Mark Mitchell returns to Missouri a week after Kentucky commitment
content:
A week after committing to Kentucky, forward Mark Mitchell has instead reenrolled at Missouri and plans to play for the Tigers next season, according to multiple reports.

Mitchell’s late switch would appear to be in part due to the SEC’s announcement late last week that the league would enforce its intraconference transfer rules, which prevent players from transferring to another SEC school outside of the NCAA’s approved spring portal window.

Mitchell, a fifth-year player who gained another season of eligibility in August after a Kentucky judge granted him a temporary restraining order, is subject to that rule. Rather than fight the SEC on that, Kentucky and Mitchell opted not to take on another legal battle, clearing the way for the 6-foot-8 forward to return to Dennis Gates’ Missouri program.

It’s a massive loss for Kentucky and a significant win for Missouri, which now has one of the deeper and more versatile frontcourts in the SEC. Mitchell earned All-SEC honors last season after averaging 18.2 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. He played in the NBA Summer League with the Denver Nuggets but did not sign a contract.

Kentucky envisioned Mitchell as the final piece of a potential Final Four contender. While UK coach Mark Pope already added former Iowa State sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic on the wing this offseason, Mitchell’s interior scoring and defensive length would’ve further elevated UK in the national hierarchy.

Without Mitchell, Kentucky is back to being a fringe top-25 team built around Momcilovic, Washington transfer Zoom Diallo, Furman transfer Alex Wilkins and rising sophomore Malachi Moreno, who returned to school after going through the NBA Draft process in May.

Missouri had already built an impressive frontcourt with former Kansas forward Bryson Tiller, former Tennessee center Jaylen Carey and incoming top-25 recruit Toni Bryant, but Mitchell is probably the best of the bunch and immediately makes Gates’ team a dark horse SEC contender.

Along with that rebuilt frontcourt, Gates welcomed top-five recruit Jason Crowe Jr. and Providence transfer Jamier Jones on the wing this summer, setting Missouri up to be a borderline top-15 team in the preseason.
